candidate_relations.reason: The clinical picture—synthetic cannabis use, prior ischemic stroke and MI, now seizures with diffuse bilateral cortical and subcortical edema on MRI—points to RCVS as the unifying diagnosis. Seizures are a manifestation/complication of RCVS, and synthetic cannabis is the precipitant, but the candidate label stops at the symptomatic level and omits the core vascular diagnosis. It is compatible with the etiology but lacks the required specificity of RCVS.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Identifies the seizure manifestation and synthetic cannabis as the trigger/etiology but does not name the underlying vascular syndrome (RCVS) that explains the diffuse bilateral cortical/subcortical edema and the prior stroke/MI pattern

case_quality_flags: Diffuse bilateral cortical/subcortical edema pattern is more consistent with RCVS-associated PRES (posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome) overlap than classic RCVS presentation; however, reference diagnosis is RCVS and the case context supports it given recurrent vascular events with synthetic cannabis use.
